_comment: Varnfell lore. The Elder God inscriptions are read by bumping each oracle's ruined statue.

lore.name: The Elder God of Time
paragraphs: Time was the first god to count and gave the world a before and an after. Time brought the promise that everything would come into existence and provided beginnings and an endings.
The area has  hourglasses discarded around the statue's  feet. Notably, the sand in every one of them has long since run out.

lore.name: The Elder God of Space
paragraphs: After the Varn, Space woke first and made room, and extended into every direction.
The pillars here are arranged in the way that must have once defined the area of this shrine, but this space is otherwise empty.

lore.name: The Elder God of Fire
paragraphs: Fire was born from deep beneath the world. Fire fueled the forge of the world, made big mountains and carved out the world.
These braziers were tended for a thousand years with great care, but now they have long gone out.

lore.name: The Elder God of Water
paragraphs: Water came to cool the world. Folk wisdoms says that rivers are the tears of the fallen god that became the world.
The moat around this shrine has never once run dry.

lore.name: The Elder God of Air
paragraphs: Air is the Varn's last breath. It fills the world and carries every word ever spoken up to the sky, but nothing answers back.
Offerings here were whispered, never spoken aloud. If you listen carefully, you can hear faint whispers traveling around the ruins of this place.

lore.name: The Elder God of Earth
paragraphs: Earth is the very body of Varn itself and in this body rests many secrets yet to be unmasked.
The stone of this hall was never cut, the pieces look as if they were pulled directly from the world itself.

lore.name: The Elder God of Birth
paragraphs: Birth dared to create something new from the scattered remains of a dead god. Every seed and every child was counted among its works.
Mothers once walked here barefoot to ask its blessing. The garden still grows without them.

lore.name: The Elder God of Death
paragraphs: Death rose up to strike down everything else. Everything in Varnfell exists, but pays a price at the end when Death arrived to collect the dues of the Varn.
The graves here face downward so the dead can find their way home.

lore.name: The Elder God of Love
paragraphs: Love is friend to friend, kin to kin, oath to oath. Love is the binding force that pushes things back together.
Two names were carved on every stone of this court. Most have worn away.

lore.name: The Elder God of Hate
paragraphs: Hate is the great separator and cause of great pain. Hate is that which causes the destruction of what needs to be cast aside.
Folklore says that a great war of the gods began in this shrine. The broken walls do not argue.

lore.name: The Elder God of Good
paragraphs: All that is beautiful and right in this world is Good.
Its temple was the last to fall and the least damaged, but it is now completely vacant. Sounds ring hollow over the broken stone artifacts.

lore.name: The Elder God of Evil
paragraphs: Destroyed families, weakened kingdoms, blight and famine all come from the echo of the god of Evil.
The throne behind this statue is in a perfect state as if the item was created yesterday, yet the remains of everything else in the area is destroyed and full of blight.
